name: Package Management
description: Install or uninstall an APK by URL, update the panel's System WebView, and neutralize intrusive vendor packages. Requires root; no vendor signature pinning or auto-update machinery — you choose what to install.
author: David Coulson

settings.title: APK to install (URL)
settings.description: HTTPS URL to an APK. Trigger the Install action below to download and install it.

settings.title: Uninstall: pick a known package
settings.description: Common vendor/test packages, so you don't have to type one. Run the Uninstall package action to apply. Anything typed into the field below takes priority over this pick. Uninstalling is not reversible without a factory reset or reflash — prefer taming if you only want an app to stop interfering.

settings.title: Package to uninstall
settings.description: Overrides the dropdown above when non-empty. Use for anything not listed there.

settings.title: System WebView: known-good build
settings.description: Pick "Recommended for this panel" to let the plugin choose from the panel's own ABI and Android version. Builds are ha-paneld's, verified on real panels. An explicit pick overrides the recommendation; one whose ABI can't run here is refused. Not Google-signed — a panel that still gets WebView through Play should use Play. See the README.

settings.title: System WebView APK (URL)
settings.description: HTTPS URL to a com.android.webview build for this panel's ABI. Overrides the dropdown above when non-empty. Trigger the Update WebView action below.

settings.title: elclcd OTA updater
settings.description: ELC "Firmware Upgrade", the vendor OTA updater. Disable to stop the panel auto-applying vendor firmware that re-adds bloat — and, on some images, re-enables ADB. Verified on rk3576; ha-paneld disables it on smt1019 and wf1589t. Package: com.elclcd.otaupdater

settings.title: elclcd keepalive service
settings.description: ELC "CommonKeepAlive", the vendor's process-resurrector — this is what undoes taming anything else, so tame it alongside whatever else you tame on these panels. Verified on rk3576; ha-paneld disables it on smt1019. Package: com.elclcd.commonkeepalive

settings.title: Vendor RGB LED demo (PwmLightDemo)
settings.description: The only package ha-paneld rates *recommended* rather than optional. Its boot-started foreground service continuously cycles colours through /dev/ledjni, which fights any LED control of your own. Tame this if you use the Rockchip LED plugin. Package: com.gulukai.pwmlightdemo

settings.title: Factory test: DeviceTest
settings.description: Generic factory device-test app, in /odm persist so it survives a factory reset. Diagnostic only. Verified on rk3576 and px30; ha-paneld disables it on smt1019 and wf1589t. Package: com.DeviceTest

settings.title: Factory test: burn-in Stresstest
settings.description: Factory hardware stress-test ("burn-in") tool, a priv-app. Production-line QA with no role on a deployed panel. Verified on rk3576 and px30; ha-paneld disables it on wf1589t. Package: com.cghs.stresstest

settings.title: Factory test: elc smt_test
settings.description: ELC factory QA tool, in /odm persist so it survives a factory reset. Verified on rk3576 and px30; ha-paneld disables it on smt1019. Package: com.elc.smt_test

settings.title: Factory test: Rockchip devicetest
settings.description: Rockchip SoC factory device-test suite. Diagnostic only. From ha-paneld's wf1589t profile; not present on the panels tested here, in which case this toggle does nothing. Package: com.rockchip.devicetest

settings.title: Factory test: smatek test
settings.description: Factory/QA leftover. Verified present on rk3576 and px30 panels here; this one is not in ha-paneld's profiles. Package: com.smatek.test

settings.title: Factory test: Tuya devicetest
settings.description: Tuya factory device-test app, in /odm so it persists across a factory reset. Diagnostic only. From ha-paneld's tpa10 profile. Package: com.tuya.devicetest

settings.title: Xinch SmartIoT control app
settings.description: SmartOS/Tuya IoT control app — redundant alongside Home Assistant. From ha-paneld's tpa10 profile. Package: com.smartos.xinch.smartiot

settings.title: Xinch smart-home control app
settings.description: SmartOS/Tuya smart-home control app — redundant on a Home Assistant panel. From ha-paneld's tpa10 profile. Package: com.smartos.xinch.smarthome

settings.title: Xinch PerformanceMonitor
settings.description: Vendor diagnostic overlay app. Not needed in normal operation, and its overlay is the kind that lands on top of a dashboard. From ha-paneld's tpa10 profile. Package: com.smartos.xinch.monitor

settings.title: Tamed vendor packages
settings.description: Extra packages to tame, space or comma separated, for anything not listed above. Added to the toggles, not instead of them. Critical system packages are always refused.

settings.title: Simulation mode
settings.description: Test the controls without touching hardware or packages.
